title: What does the snowflake look like after Step one?
description: A side of one unit is cut into three equal parts, a triangle is raised over the middle part and the middle part is removed. The video counts the sides, finds the length of each side and finds the perimeter at Step one. Keeko's doubt is that the perimeter stays three units.
teaching_notes: One idea: each side becomes four sides, each one third as long, so the perimeter grows. Watch for students who think the perimeter stays the same because the bump is made from the same side.

source: Start with an equilateral triangle of side 1 unit. Find the
video_script.why: The child knows how the snowflake of {{NAME_3}} is built and now counts and measures what Step one makes.
video_script.substitution: Count the sides one old side becomes, multiply by the number of old sides, and multiply by the length of one new side.
video_script.anchor: the snowflake of {{NAME_3}} in the book, drawn at Step zero and Step one on a triangle of side one unit
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks the perimeter stays three units because the bump is made from the same side. The old side held three pieces of one third, and the bump holds four, so each side grows.
video_script.payoff_line: Step one has twelve sides, each one third of a unit, and the perimeter is four units

final_answer.spoken: twelve sides, each one third of a unit, and a perimeter of four units

names.{{NAME_3}}: Swedish mathematician who described the snowflake in 1904

hold_back: Answer: 12 sides, each 1/3 unit, perimeter 4 units
maths_rules: each side is divided into 3 equal parts of 1/3 unit
an equilateral triangle is raised over the middle part and the middle part is removed
one side becomes 4 sides: 2 old thirds plus 2 sides of the raised triangle
each new side is 1/3 unit long
perimeter = number of sides x length of one side = 12 x 1/3 = 4 units
video_script.design: One side of the triangle is shown large and changed into a bump; then the whole snowflake at Step one with its twelve sides numbered.

narration: <bookmark mark='stay'/>Step one, count the pieces that replace one side. Two outer thirds stay on the old line.
<bookmark mark='add'/>The raised triangle adds two more sides. Two plus two is four, so one side becomes four sides.

beats.on_screen: Number of sides = old sides x 4 = 3 x 4 = 12

marks.rule: the line number of sides equals old sides times 4 is written
marks.calc: 3 x 4 = 12 is written and the twelve sides of the shape are numbered

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step two, count all the sides. The triangle has three sides, and each becomes four sides.
<bookmark mark='calc'/>Three times four is twelve sides.

beats.on_screen: Length of each new side = 1/3 unit

marks.third: each new side is marked 1/3 unit
marks.same: the raised triangle's sides are shown equal to the middle part

narration: <bookmark mark='third'/>Step three, find the length of each side. The outer pieces are each one third of the old side.
<bookmark mark='same'/>The raised triangle is equilateral, so its sides equal the middle part. Every side is one third of a unit.

beats.on_screen: Perimeter = number of sides x length of one side = 12 x 1/3 = 4 units

marks.rule: the line perimeter equals number of sides times length of one side is written
marks.calc: 12 x 1/3 = 4 is written with the unit

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step four, find the perimeter. It is the number of sides times the length of one side.
<bookmark mark='calc'/>Twelve times one third is four units.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 12 sides, each 1/3 unit, perimeter 4 units
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Step one has twelve sides, each one third of a unit, and the perimeter is four units.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the perimeter stays three units, because the bump is made from the same side.
<bookmark mark='lay'/>Lay the four pieces of one bump in a line. They run past the end of the old side.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The old side held three thirds, and the bump holds four thirds. Each side grows, so the perimeter grows.
